context: A teacher walks a uni student through an archaeology paper
purpose: Teach: 亡命/損傷/神聖/考古学/試練/畜産/粒子/仮名

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 論文、考古学と亡命知識人の交流を扱うんですね。
lines.en: Your paper's on archaeology and cultural exchange with exiled intellectuals, then.
lines.style: Warm curiosity, slightly leaning forward. Genuine interest in the topic. Measured pace, giving space for him to expand. The tone of a teacher who reads and remembers.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。神聖視された遺跡の損傷、試練の歴史として書きます。
lines.en: Yes. I'm framing the damage to sacred sites as historical testimony — a record of disruption and loss.
lines.style: Quiet intensity. Slight pause before 'testimony' — he's choosing his words carefully. Respectful of the weight of what he's describing. No rush.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 畜産遺構の比較、面白そうですね。
lines.en: Comparing livestock structures across sites — that's a really interesting angle.
lines.style: Nod in the voice. Genuine surprise at the specificity. Warm acknowledgment that he's thought this through. Open, inviting him to say more.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 粒子レベルの分析手法、最新の論文を引用します。
lines.en: I'll cite the latest papers on particle-level analysis methods to ground the methodology.
lines.style: Methodical, slightly faster now — he's confident here. Precise articulation. The relief of talking about concrete steps he knows how to take.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 文献名の仮名表記、丁寧に整えて。
lines.en: Just make sure the phonetic readings for all your source titles are clean and consistent.
lines.style: Gentle directive, not lecturing. The tone of someone who's seen overlooked details derail good work. Steady, maternal without being patronizing.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.style: Quiet, sincere commitment. Not defensive. The relief of clear instruction. Short breath, settled.
